candidate.title: MIRA
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina schematic of the methylated-CpG island recovery assay (MIRA): genomic DNA fragmentation, MBD2B/MBD3L1 affinity binding, glutathione-bead isolation, and the combined DNA purification/PCR amplification endpoint. The title and collection caption identify one MIRA schematic; catalogue discussion of MIRA-chip and MIRA-seq describes downstream uses and does not depict alternative target workflows. Sequencing and array analysis are downstream interfaces, not drawn operations.

evidence.locator: Description, target enrichment and downstream analysis
evidence.quote: (MIRA) uses the high affinity of a methylated-CpG-binding protein complex (MBD2B and MBD3L1) to enrich regions with methylated CpG dinucleotides.
evidence.rationale: The selection acts on whole genomic fragments before purification and PCR; the diagram ends in ordinary DNA rather than a base-converted methylation code. operations.label: Isolate on glutathione-coated beads
operations.description: Capture the DNA-bound affinity complex on glutathione-coated beads, producing a retained bead-associated DNA fraction and an excluded unbound fraction.
operations.mechanism: Interpreted capture interface: the GST-bearing binding reagent links the DNA–protein complex to the glutathione-coated bead. This interpretation uses the catalogue tag identities together with the depicted protein-mediated attachment; it does not assign an unshown covalent modification to DNA.
operations.information_effect: Enriches for methylated-CpG-containing genomic fragments and excludes the illustrated unbound fragment from the continuing route. Capture is an affinity selection, not proof of perfect biological specificity. The catalogue reports a requirement for at least two methylated CpGs per captured fragment and fragment-scale resolution; those numerical claims retain their secondary-source status.

method_scopes.rationale: All four operations apply to the single MIRA schematic named by the card title, the image title icon, and the verified collection-page caption. MIRA is the expanded name methylated-CpG island recovery assay. MIRA-chip and MIRA-seq are catalogue-described downstream uses, with neither a separate branch nor an alternative workflow in this drawing. The GST-MBD2B/His-MBD3L1 and glutathione-bead implementation is supported by the catalogue and image; primary application papers support the shared enrichment architecture without establishing that every commercial-kit MIRA implementation has this exact interface. The common DNA purification/PCR amplification caption stays one broad operation. No historical priority or interchangeability of variants is asserted.

checks.rationale: Accept at the declared schematic scope. Independently checked all eight states, four operations, eleven material routes, the single method scope and five PaperMatches against the image and supplied evidence. Every depicted transformation and the excluded unbound fraction are represented. Input/output identities and attachment changes agree across the entire retained route; genuine reagent addition and affinity separation justify the multi-input/output operations. The broad recovery/amplification block preserves the level of the drawing. The selected DNA sequence is the eventual readout carrier for regional methylation enrichment; base-specific methylation calls, perfect specificity and unshown library chemistry are not asserted. The primary applications support the MIRA core without being used to certify the exact catalogue GST/glutathione implementation. Both incorrect reference links and abstract-only limits are explicitly retained in the PaperMatches. No consequential scientific omission, unsupported assertion, required correction or blocking architecture question remains.
